races.title: State House, District 68
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: David Willis
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 68 (Union County) since 2021. Appalachian State graduate (1996). Former Bank of America senior vice president and owner of a Kiddie Academy preschool in Charlotte. Chairs the House Appropriations subcommittee on Education.
cands.gaps: I could not find where David Willis was born or raised, or the year he moved to North Carolina. I found no statements or actions by him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, gun laws or abortion. His campaign site lists bills he says he authored or helped pass, but the pages I could read did not include legislative records confirming his sponsorship or role. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2024 or 2026. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in the pages reviewed.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2021, including as vice chair of the full Appropriations Committee. Earlier he spent over 15 years in manufacturing, banking and finance (Bank of America senior vice president) and now owns a preschool franchise.
qual.why: Five years of legislative service that includes budget-writing work, plus a banking and finance career and business ownership. Committee chairmanships were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: Five years of legislative service that includes budget-writing work, plus a banking and finance career and business ownership. Committee chairmanships were not counted toward the score.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he was primary sponsor of the 2023 Charter School Omnibus (SL 2023-107) and the Charter School Review Board law (SL 2023-110), the latter enacted over the Governor's veto. This is his own account and I did not check it against legislative records.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site lists the Criminal Illegal Alien Enforcement Act among bills he 'helped pass.' This is his own claim and his specific role is not documented in the pages I read.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site lists the LEO Special Separation Allowance among bills he 'helped pass.' This is his own claim and his specific role is not documented in the pages I read.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

cands.name: Derek Warriner
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina House District 68 in 2026. Healthcare executive for about 15 years, at Philips Healthcare (2011-2023) and Riverain Technologies (2023-present). Studied finance at Santa Clara University. Has held no elected office.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Derek Warriner was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. His campaign site lists a high school in Dallas, Texas, but does not say where he grew up. He has held no public office, so there are no legislative actions to report. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws or abortion. The 2001 reality-TV win and his volunteer work appear only on his own campaign site, and we could not confirm them elsewhere.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Healthcare industry executive for about 15 years (Philips Healthcare 2011-2023, Riverain Technologies 2023-present), with a finance degree from Santa Clara University. He lists earlier work as a server, bartender, fundraiser and newspaper ad salesman, and says he was president of a homeowners association.
qual.why: A long business and management career puts him in the middle band. He has no legislative service and no record of local elected office, and a homeowners association presidency is not public office.
qual.label: A long business and management career puts him in the middle band. He has no legislative service and no record of local elected office, and a homeowners association presidency is not public office.

clean-money.evidence: Pledges to fight on day one for a law barring any corporation doing business in North Carolina from spending money on politics, including Super PAC donations.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)
